## 2. Physical command and reset operators, not a decoder relabeling
For an absolute target v the reference-frame Hamiltonian is a direct sum of pairs r_g<->e_(g,v), g!=v. Its permanent-gauge image is exactly

    Omega[u_v u_g dagger tensor |e_(g,v)><r_g|+h.c.].

The physical reset J_(a,b)=sqrt(kappa)|r_b><e_(a,b)| is clock-only because BOTH endpoint frames equal b. Every native memory term is also conjugated by the same fixed G, once and permanently. Conjugating only the command drive would not establish the theorem.

All resets are SEPARATE Lindblad channels. This is load-bearing. With m>=3 and final target v=0, coherently merging resets into

    J_1=sqrt(kappa)|r_1>(<e_(0,1)|+<e_(2,1)|)

would leave the stale state (|e_(0,1)>-|e_(2,1)>)/sqrt(2) dark. The held-target Hamiltonian has no action on these stale labels, so this would be an exact counterexample to uniform convergence. The frozen source explicitly excludes that different reservoir model.

Likewise, an arbitrary program-frame reset between unequal frames would become a DATA-active physical jump under G. The repaired transition model does not assume those extra dissipators: only bounded program Hamiltonian interpolation/selection is used, while the same separate clock-only resets stay on. This preserves the declared physical resource class.

For projective Clifford labels, controlled global phases cannot simply disappear from the clock Hamiltonian. One safe extension uses fixed lifts and exact products u_v u_g dagger; a finite central extension is another. Phase-stripped products leave known scalar phases on clock edges and require the corresponding phased Gramian, though the DATA-free property can survive. The concrete exact GL(2,2) representation avoids this optional issue entirely.

## 6. Absolute cumulative targets, not repeated relative application
A command v asks the physical register to approach absolute frame v. Reissuing v to already settled r_v does nothing; it does not apply v again. To realize a requested sequence of relative gates a_1,...,a_K, the external controller must command cumulative elements v_j=a_j...a_1 in the declared multiplication order.

When native registers are ready and programs are settled at r_g, physical DATA is U_g Enc(rho)U_g dagger. Settling at r_v changes that physical frame to U_v; relative to the prior settled logical state this is U_v U_g dagger. This is an actual physical change produced by the onsite command Hamiltonians, not a relabeling performed by the decoder.

The word is finite-group/classically compressible. If only the final output matters, an equally informed ordinary controller can compute the final group element and schedule that single layer after protected storage. The absence of a separate K-error term is not a quantum computational advantage. If intermediate physical targets must also be available, their transition/settling times contribute to T. The theorem does not model repeated destructive decoding/reinsertion, adaptive measurements or conditional feedback.

## 8. Quantitative endpoint and scaling limits
With M_col<=C_col N, m_N=ceil(beta N) and p_tail<beta/(e C_col), subset union gives

    Tr rho_P(T)1_(|H|>=m_N)
       <=[(e C_col/beta)p_tail]^m_N
       <=C exp(-b_prog N).

The event is empty if m_N exceeds the column count. The ceil convention safely overbounds the complement at integer beta N. No memory-weight tail is needed because P already enforces its radius deterministically.

Gentle projection on the good current-label set costs at most twice the square root of this tail. The exact suffix/frame unitaries and fixed recovery are contractions. Adding the one full-versus-killed difference and lost mass yields

    gate error<=2 epsilon_mem(T)+2sqrt(delta_prog)+delta_prog,

which gives the bound in Section 0. It is uniform with references and the retained common bath. There is no per-command reset, per-command projection, or sum of restart errors; T still grows when actual transitions/dwells are required.

Fixed b and Gamma are essential. Onsite dimensions, number of independently resolved reset channels, target-control catalog, Pauli spread and forest support do not grow with command count K. This says nothing comparable for unbounded block sets and changing CNOT partners: a naive CNOT chain can spread one Pauli over K+1 blocks. Grouping them into one site or recording unbounded frame history would violate the fixed-resource premise. That is an obstruction to this naive extension, not a no-go theorem for all fault-tolerant handoffs.
